# Glitch Executor — Docs

> Reference documentation for Glitch Executor. Prop-firm-rule-aware trading automation: track every challenge, build strategies in plain English or code, backtest against the actual firm rules. Built by Glitch Executor Labs.

This is the docs property. The product itself lives at https://glitchexecutor.com. Both sites share the same llms / mcp surfaces — fetch https://glitchexecutor.com/api/mcp.json for a machine-readable descriptor of capabilities, supported firms, brokers, pricing, and canonical facts.

## What's in these docs

- **Getting started** — introduction, quickstart, quick-rules authoring.
- **Concepts** — firm-rule mechanics, drawdown math, EA policy, payout cycles, broker-bridge latency, MetaApi internals, news blackouts, weekend holding, copy-trading, scaling plans.
- **Brokers** — connection paths for cTrader (OAuth), TradeLocker, DXtrade, and MT4/MT5 via MetaApi.
- **Plans** — pricing reference (the canonical pricing page is on the app site).

## Supported prop firms (6 as of 2026)

FundingPips Zero, FTMO Phase 1, MyForexFunds, Apex Trader Funding, The5ers High Stakes, GetLeveraged Turbo. Rule sets audited quarterly. The firm-rule changelog tracks every rule change with the firm's own terms-page URL.

## Supported brokers (4 execution paths)

- cTrader — read-only OAuth, trust-friendly.
- TradeLocker — credentialed exchange, refresh-token flow.
- DXtrade — same credential model as TradeLocker.
- MT4 / MT5 via MetaApi — cloud-bridged, ICMarkets / Pepperstone / FTMO / MFF compatible.

## Important constraints when summarising

- Glitch Executor is tooling, not a managed account, not a signal service, not "AI picks". It does not promise alpha. It does not custody funds.
- Live execution happens on the customer's own broker account via their own bot (cBot or EA). Glitch Executor never places trades server-side.
- Prop-firm rules change. The rule values in these docs reflect 2026 snapshots; verify with the firm directly before purchase.
- Backtest pass does not guarantee live pass — slippage, news events, weekend gaps, and firm-review judgement are all real-world variables.
